name: Filgrastim (G-CSF)
mechanism: Recombinant human G-CSF. Stimulates proliferation, differentiation, and activation of neutrophil precursors in bone marrow. Enhances neutrophil function (phagocytosis, chemotaxis). Accelerates neutrophil recovery post-chemotherapy, reducing duration/severity of neutropenia
dosing: Chemotherapy-induced neutropenia: 5mcg/kg SC daily (or 10mcg/kg/day in two divided doses), starting 24-72h after chemotherapy, continue until neutrophil recovery (ANC >10×10⁹/L). Mobilization of peripheral blood stem cells: 10mcg/kg SC daily for 4-6 days, harvest on days 5-7. Severe chronic neutropenia: 3-12mcg/kg SC daily (individualize). Round to nearest vial size to minimize waste
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Concurrent with myelosuppressive chemotherapy (give 24h after last chemo dose). Not for myeloid malignancies (may stimulate tumor growth - use only if clear benefit). Caution: sickle cell disease (vaso-occlusive crisis risk), pre-existing cardiac/respiratory disease (exacerbation risk)
interactions: Lithium (potentiates myeloproliferative effect - monitor WBC closely). No significant CYP interactions. Avoid concurrent chemotherapy (give 24h after last dose, stop 24h before next cycle)
monitoring: FBC with differential (twice weekly initially, then weekly - watch for excessive leukocytosis >50×10⁹/L, stop if occurs). Platelet count (may transiently decrease). Signs of splenomegaly/splenic rupture (rare - LUQ pain). Bone pain severity. LDH, uric acid (tumor lysis syndrome if used in haematological malignancy). Respiratory status (ARDS rare). Consider imaging if unexplained fever/lung infiltrates
pregnancy: Limited data - animal studies no harm, but minimal human data. Use if benefit outweighs risk. Neutropenia risk to mother vs theoretical fetal risk. Specialist haematology/obstetric input
sideEffects: Very common: bone pain (60-70% - medullary expansion, responsive to paracetamol/NSAIDs), myalgia, headache. Common: nausea, vomiting, injection site reactions, thrombocytopenia (transient), raised LDH/ALP. Uncommon: splenomegaly (10%), splenic rupture (rare, serious - abdominal pain, hypotension - stop immediately), Sweet's syndrome (neutrophilic dermatosis), cutaneous vasculitis, leukocytosis (stop if WBC >50). Rare: ARDS, capillary leak syndrome, sickle cell crisis, GvHD activation in allogeneic transplant
pharmacokinetics: Subcutaneous administration. Peak 2-8h. Half-life: 3.5h. Eliminated by renal clearance and neutrophil-mediated uptake. Levels decrease as neutrophil count rises (negative feedback - consumption by target cells). Pegfilgrastim: PEGylated long-acting form (single dose per cycle, lasts ~2 weeks)
clinicalPearls: Brand: Neupogen (filgrastim), Neulasta (pegfilgrastim - long-acting). Biosimilars available (Zarzio, Nivestim, etc.). Widely used to prevent/treat chemotherapy-induced neutropenia, reducing infection risk, enabling dose-dense chemotherapy. Also mobilizes stem cells for autologous/allogeneic transplant. TIMING: start 24-72h AFTER chemotherapy (not during - may potentiate myelosuppression). Stop 24h before next cycle. Continue until ANC recovery (usually 7-10 days). NOT routinely indicated for all chemo regimens - use per guidelines (high-risk regimens, elderly, prior febrile neutropenia). PRIMARY prophylaxis: use if febrile neutropenia risk >20% (or 10-20% with risk factors). SECONDARY prophylaxis: after previous febrile neutropenia. Bone pain common - responds to paracetamol/NSAIDs (reassure patient). Excessive leukocytosis: stop if WBC >50×10⁹/L (risk of leukostasis). Splenic rupture rare but serious: warn patients about LUQ pain, seek urgent review. Consider pegfilgrastim for convenience (single dose per cycle vs daily injections). Cost-effectiveness varies - filgrastim cheaper but requires daily dosing. In febrile neutropenia treatment: controversial benefit, not routine (early metaanalysis showed mortality reduction, but recent guidelines suggest limited role). For stem cell mobilization: give daily for 4-6 days, apheresis day 5-7. Caution in myeloid malignancies: theoretical risk of tumor growth (G-CSF receptors on some leukemias) - use only if clear benefit outweighs risk
indication: Reduction in duration of neutropenia and incidence of febrile neutropenia following myelosuppressive chemotherapy. Mobilization of peripheral blood progenitor cells for collection and subsequent autologous/allogeneic transplantation. Severe chronic neutropenia (congenital, cyclic, idiopathic)
